articleTitle: Malaysia renewable energy policy and its impact on regional countries
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: By 2025, Malaysia wants to incorporate 20% renewable energy into its overall energy mix. To achieve this, the country has created a variety of laws and programmes that support the expansion of renewable energy sources. The main policies will be examined and critiqued in this article. the National Renewable Energy Policy and Action Plan (NREPAP), the Feed-in Tariff (FiT) programme, Net Energy Metering (NEM), the Green Technology Financing Scheme (GTFS), and the Sustainable Energy Development Authority (SEDA), are a few of the major policies being examined for their effects on the regional nations. The goal of Malaysia's renewable energy strategy is to lessen the nation's reliance on fossil fuels while promoting the growth of renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: Research on the aerodynamic characteristics of wind turbine under coupled pitching motion and yaw error
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: The coupling of floating platform motion and yaw can cause complex aerodynamic characteristics of the rotor, which can affect the power generation and safety of the turbine. In this research, the free vortex method was used to investigate the change of power and aerodynamic characteristics of floating wind turbine under yaw conditions when influenced by pitching motion. The research results showed that as the yaw angle increased, the output power decreased in a second-order cosine function and the thrust decreased in a first-order cosine function; The minimum value of normal force coefficient had a phase shift from -5 to 15 degrees; The decomposition of the normal force coefficient curve revealed that the amplitude of the fundamental frequency and second harmonic components were positively correlated with the yaw angle, while the third harmonic component was not correlated with the yaw angle; among them, the coupling of wind turbine rotation and pitching motion resulted in a higher frequency component of the normal force coefficient relative to the motion frequency. These research findings have guiding significance for the aerodynamic design of deep-sea floating wind turbines.

articleTitle: Risk prediction of sub-synchronous oscillation based on the black-box impedance model of DFIG for multiple operating conditions
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: In recent years, the oscillation problem of renewable energy power generation systems has seriously threatened the safe operation of power systems. For example, a new type of sub-synchronous oscillation (SSO) is caused by interactions with Doubly-fed Induction Generator (DFIG) and series complement oscillation. At present, the impedance method is often used to analyse the stability of the system under specific conditions, but it can't predict the oscillation risk of the DFIG under the multiple operating conditions of sub-synchronous oscillation. To study the influence of general conditions on the system, this paper firstly proposed a stability criterion method based on the impedance network model and analyse the oscillation risk of DFIG by stability criterion. Then, based on the identification method, this article obtains the impedance model of DFIG, and the impedance model for multiple operating conditions is constructed by fitting the impedance curve of typical operating conditions. Finally, the sub-synchronous oscillation risk prediction method based on the black-box impedance model of DFIG for multiple operating conditions is verified by the simulation, which can significantly improve the study for the oscillation risk prediction of SSO.

articleTitle: Graph computing and graph database applications in power system online dispatch
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: In the new types of power systems, characterized by the dominance of renewable energies, uncertain resources such as wind and solar power will play a significant role in power generation. However, the inherent unpredictability and fluctuation of these renewable sources make the operating conditions complex and variable. To address this, intelligent online dispatch applications that integrate optimization and artificial intelligence techniques need to be implemented. In terms of online dispatch, estimating system states and optimizing resources require computing a large number of variables while adhering to operating constraints. Graph computing and graph database technologies have shown promising results in power system online analysis. This paper analyzes the applications of these graph computing techniques to enhance online dispatch and provides a graph computing based-grid online analysis architecture. This architecture offers a range of online situational awareness applications and decision-making support.

articleTitle: Anomaly data enhancement and detection for charging piles considering generative adversarial network
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: The accuracy of anomaly detection results is affected by factors such as low proportion of abnormal data samples and imbalanced distribution. To address the issue that the current abnormal data detection model for charging piles depends on the quality of abnormal data samples in the training set, this paper proposes a charging pile abnormal data augmentation method based on Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) and the corresponding abnormal data detection model. The proposed method first improves the traditional GAN by introducing the unsaturated activation function Leaky ReLU (LR) and proposes charging pile abnormal data augmentation method based on LR-GAN to enhance the abnormal data in the training set. Then, the LR-GAN augmented training set is used as input for the Random Forests (RF) model to establish a charging pile abnormal data detection model based on LR-GAN-RF to detect abnormal data in the charging pile charging dataset. Finally, different charging pile anomaly data sets are used to validate the feasibility and effectiveness of this method, which is verified to be highly feasible.

articleTitle: Optimal allocation of distributed synchronous condenser for SSO mitigation
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Weak grid connection is one of the main causes for the sub-synchronous oscillations (SSOs) of renewable power generation systems (RPGSs). In this paper, the allocation of distributed synchronous condensers (DSCs) is optimized to mitigate this kind of SSO. First, impedance model of the RPGS with DSCs integrated is established. Second, an optimization model for the allocation of DSCs to mitigate SSO is established. The objective function is to minimize the cost of the DSCs. The constraints include: 1) the satisfaction of the generalized Nyquist criterion under different operating conditions, and 2) the limitation on the capacity of the condenser. Finally, the optimal allocation problem for an example RPGS is solved by using the particle swarm optimization. The effectiveness of the optimized deployment of DSCs in mitigating SSO is verified with electromagnetic simulations.

articleTitle: Reliability analysis of phase differential protection for PV outgoing circuit fault
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: In the photovoltaic connected distribution system, the photovoltaic is connected to the AC grid through the inverter. It brings great challenges to the protection of the AC outgoing line. When a fault occurs on the AC side, the fault current phase presents a controlled characteristic. The control mode of the inverter has great influence on the fault current, and the negative sequence current suppression of the inverter will further affect the fault current phase. Differential protection mainly uses the current and phase relationship between photovoltaic side and grid side for fault discrimination. Due to the large difference in fault current between photovoltaic side and grid side, it is difficult to ensure reliable operation of differential protection. This paper aims at the scenario of photovoltaic connecting to AC power grid. The phase characteristics of photovoltaic side current are analyzed with inverter control mode. The differential protection sensitivity in this scenario is analyzed by simulation.

articleTitle: Smart city initiatives in Malaysia and Southeast Asia
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Malaysia has been actively promoting and implementing various initiatives, programs, and efforts to develop smart cities across the country. Various collaborative efforts involving government agencies, local authorities, private sector entities, and academia are contributing to smart city development in Malaysia. Partnerships and collaborations aim to share expertise, resources, and best practices, fostering innovation and effective implementation of smart city projects. The Malaysian government has introduced policies and regulations to support smart city development. These include guidelines on data privacy and security, standards for interoperability and connectivity, and incentives for technology adoption and investment in smart city projects. Academic institutions, research organizations, and industry players in Malaysia are actively engaged in research and development activities related to smart cities. These efforts focus on areas such as IoT, data analytics, sustainable technologies, and citizen engagement, aiming to drive innovation and provide evidence-based solutions for smart city development. These initiatives, programs, and collaborative efforts reflect Malaysia's commitment to embracing technology, sustainability, and innovation in its journey toward developing smart cities. The government continues to promote and support the implementation of smart city projects across the country.

articleTitle: Self-scheduling problem of a renewable community aggregator trading in energy and reserve markets
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: In this paper, a renewable community aggregator (RCA) performs joint energy and reserve schedule considering its participation in both energy and reserve markets. RCA consists of gas turbine, electricity storage, and prosumers with flexible electricity demands and controllable roof-top PV panels. To provide a reasonable schedule and represent the contribution of each device and prosumer inside RCA, this paper models the reserve providing ability of all devices and prosumers in detail with their own technical constraints. Two numerical cases are set to analyse the relationship between energy schedule and reserve schedule, and to calculate the commercial profit of providing reserve services.

articleTitle: Flexibility and economic analysis of high pressure industrial heating system upgrading scheme for a cogeneration unit
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Flexibility upgrading of co-generation units is one of the most challenging undertakings confronting the power industry. A configuration of high pressure industrial heating steam from the hot reheat steam source is introduced, which will induce high degree of coupling between heating and power generation and severely hamper the cogeneration unit peak load regulating capacity. A novel flexibility upgrading scheme is proposed, which adopts turbine main steam as the steam source. Model-based software EBSILON is employed for performance simulation of one 350MW co-generation unit under various industrial steam flow conditions. Results indicate that utilizing the upgrading scheme, heating and power generation can be decoupled under various conditions, mitigating minimum power output by around 50MW. Further analysis demonstrates how the efficiency of HP and IP turbines varies with power output under the two schemes. There exists a cross point in the heat rate curves of the two schemes. Below the power output of this cross point, the upgrading scheme accomplishes superior heat rate performance. The respective cross point power outputs are 300MW, 280MW, and 240MW when the industrial steam flow rates are 50t/h, 80t/h, and 100t/h, respectively. This provides the prospect of achieving superior operational economy by judicious switching between two schemes.

articleTitle: Coordinated asymmetric fault ride-through control scheme in large scale renewable power integration system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: As the proportion of renewable power connected to the grid increasing, the integration of large renewable power plants (RPPs) connected to weak grid scenarios has attracted widespread attention. Existing LVRT standards cannot meet the asymmetric voltage support requirements of weak grids during asymmetric system faults. In large scale renewable power plants, the coordination of multiple plants with different controllable states to maximize asymmetric voltage support is a pressing technical challenge. To this end, this study proposes a novel fault coordinated asymmetric LVRT control method for the large-scale renewable power plants integration system. A unit-level fault control strategy in RPP is first constructed for independent control of positive and negative sequence active and reactive power. The positive and negative sequence fault controllable boundary planes of each RPP is constructed, and the controllable margins in different RPPs are coordinated to maximise the positive sequence voltage and suppress the negative sequence voltage of the system. Simulation results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: PLL parameter flexible control strategy for improving transient stability performance
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Phase Locked Loop (PLL), while simulating the steady state output characteristics of a conventional Synchronous generator (SG), will also face similar transient stability problems as SG. Compared with SG, the strong non-linearity of PLL makes its transient stability analysis more complicated. Based on this, an Equal Proportional Area Criterion (EPAC) based on the flexible control of the equivalent rotational inertia is proposed to provide guidance for the control of the equivalent rotational inertia of the PLL; finally, a change in the parameters of the PLL proportional integrator is proposed to improve the PLL transient stability. The phase locked loop is an important link between the VSC and the grid, but its dynamic characteristics are complex and prone to transient instability under fault conditions, endangering the safe and stable operation of the VSC. Existing research on PLLs often focuses on steady-state conditions and cannot guide the transient regulation under fault conditions. To this end, this paper firstly analyses the transient characteristics of the PLL under fault conditions and obtains the influence of key parameters on the dynamic characteristics of the PLL. Secondly, with the help of the equal proportional area rule, a flexi-ble control method for PLL control parameters is proposed to improve the transient stability performance of VSC and enhance the transient stability margin of the system. Finally, the correctness of the theory and the proposed method are verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Study on the modelling method based on testing data of the frequency control electromechanical transient model of doubly-fed wind turbine
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: It is important to study the electromechanical transient model of wind turbine participating in frequency regulation and its modelling method based on testing data to improve the analysis results of frequency regulation response characteristics of wind power grid-connected system. Based on this, this paper investigates the working principle of wind turbine frequency response in PSASP software, considers the principle of electromechanical transient time scale modelling, establishes the transfer function model of doubly-fed wind turbine considering inertia support and frequency response based on pitch angle adjustment, and then establishes the discrimination model for real measured signal modelling by differencing. In view of the multiple input and single output characteristics of the identification model, a model parameter identification method based on the niche particle swarm algorithm is proposed. Finally, the rationality of the proposed electromechanical transient model and the effectiveness of the parameter identification method are verified by using the active frequency disturbance of the improved WSCC-9BUS wind power system. The results of the testing data modelling show that the proposed method can realize the equivalent modelling of the frequency regulation characteristics of the doubly-fed wind turbine.

articleTitle: A deep reinforcement learning grid dispatching method for disconnection fault analysis and topology optimization
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: With a large number of high percentage of renewable energy resources connected to the power grid, it is challenging to apply traditional dispatching means and analysis methods to complex power system problems. To address this problem, this paper designs and implements a deep reinforcement learning grid dispatching method oriented to fault analysis and topology optimization. The agent in this algorithm is able to make decisions and execute actions to adjust the grid topology through artificial intelligence techniques under the influence of normal load fluctuations as well as randomly occurring disconnection faults to ensure safe and stable operation of the power system. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated by the IEEE 14-bus simulation validation.

articleTitle: Optimal allocation of reactive power compensation in distribution network considering distributed photovoltaic voltage regulation capability
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Large-scale distributed generation connecting to the distribution network will cause the problem of voltage overshoot, which requires additional configuration of reactive power compensation equipment. Meanwhile, different permeability of distributed power supply access and different photovoltaic-wind ratio will also affect the voltage overshoot degree of the distribution network. Considering the voltage regulation capability of distributed photovoltaic power source, this paper proposes a new optimal allocation model of reactive power compensation for distribution network, which uses distributed photovoltaic power generation as reactive power regulation equipment to participate in the voltage regulation of distribution network, so as to reduce the allocation of additional reactive power compensation equipment. Firstly, the reactive power compensation capability of distributed PV under normal operation and reasonable light abandonment is analysed respectively. On this basis, the optimal allocation model of distribution network reactive power compensation is constructed with the goal of minimizing the loss cost and reactive power compensation equipment allocation cost. Finally, an example of distribution network with different permeability and different distribution wind access ratio is constructed to verify the effectiveness of the optimization model.

articleTitle: An AC/DC bus voltage quality coordinated control strategy in hybrid microgrids
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: In hybrid AC-DC microgrids, the unbalanced voltages at the point of common coupling (PCC) cause instantaneous power fluctuations in the interlinking converters (ILCs). It will generate second-order ripple on the DC bus. Meanwhile, the integration of single-phase AC loads into the DC bus also injects second-order ripple to the DC bus, aggravating the imbalance problem at the PCC. These two issues are coupled to each other, leading to severe power quality problems. Additional equipment, such as active power filter (APF), will increase costs and cause instability. This paper proposes a coordinated control for ILC and bidirectional dc–dc converters (BDCs), which connect supercapacitor to the dc bus. The control parameters are determined according to the redundant capacity of the power converter to achieve a reasonable oscillating power sharing between the ILC and the BDC. An indicator considering both voltage imbalance at the PCC and second-order ripple is used to attain optimal coordinated control parameters. The proposed control strategy suppresses the second-order ripple in the DC bus while improving the voltage imbalance at the PCC without any additional equipment. Its effectiveness is verified through simulation results.

articleTitle: Energy hub modeling and coupling matrix automatic generation method for integrated energy system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: In Integrated Energy Systems (IES), electricity, gas, heat, and other types of energy are coupled with each other. This forms complex energy networks. A standardised Energy Hub (EH) model is the key to support the planning and operation research of IES. The coupling matrix is the core of EH modelling. The manual method of writing it in the past is not suitable for the increasingly complex IES in the future. Therefore, a method of using a computer to automatically generate the coupling matrix is urgently needed. This paper establishes a standardised EH model. On this basis, it proposes a method of automatically generating the coupling matrix by computer. This improves the computational analysis efficiency for the planning and operation of IES. First, it models the allocation, coupling and aggregation of different energies in IES. It proposes the concept of an energy flow diagram for IES. Based on the energy flow diagram, it proposes an intelligent method of generating the coupling matrix by computer. It generates the branch matrix and aggregation matrix by inputting matrices. Finally, it obtains the coupling matrix. It verifies the validity and feasibility of the model proposed in this paper through examples.

articleTitle: Research on three period time of use price mechanism of isolated microgrid considering social welfare
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Energy storage equipment and distributed renewable energy generation are necessary power source components of isolated microgrid. It is necessary to adopt the three periods time of use price mechanism to ensure that all participants in the microgrid get reasonable returns and ensure that users enjoy a fair electricity tariff. Based on the daily net load curve of microgrid, the peak-valley period division and three period time of use price model of microgrid with distributed renewable energy power generation are constructed. Among them, the peak-valley period division model is established by the goal of minimizing the average power difference between peak, flat, valley, the three periods. The three periods time of use price differences model is established by the goal of maximizing social welfare, requires the same peak-flat and flat-valley price gradient and the price difference can be maintained to meet the economy of independent operation of every component in the microgrid. The model is solved by using the particle swarm algorithm. Finally, through the analysis of examples, the correctness and rationality of the proposed models and algorithm are verified.

articleTitle: Research on harmonic analysis and DC filter configuration scheme of symmetrical unipolar topology HVDC transmission system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: The AC-to-DC technology converts the AC system to DC, improves the transmission capacity of key channels, and provides conditions for large-scale access to clean energy under the new power system. The ±200kV Yangzhou-Zhenjiang project is the first AC-to-DC project in China. Different from the symmetrical bipolar structure of conventional high-voltage direct current transmission projects, the Yangzhou-Zhenjiang project adopts symmetrical monopolar wiring, which changes the distribution of characteristic harmonics on the DC side. Therefore, it is necessary to analyze the characteristic harmonics of the Yangzhou-Zhenjiang project. On this basis, the configuration of the DC filter is studied to ensure the safe and stable operation of the entire AC-to-DC system.

articleTitle: An improved traveling wave directional criterion for line protection in MMC-HVDC grids considering frequency dependent line parameters
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: The fault direction criterion is an essential component for reliable protection of transmission lines in MMC-HVDC grids, to differentiate forward faults from backward faults. In this paper, an improved traveling wave direction criterion based on a frequency dependent parameter line model is proposed for MMC-HVDC grids. The impact of frequency dependency of line parameters in a wide frequency band during the fault period is considered using the frequency dependent parameter line model. The improved fault direction criterion is proposed based on the derivation of forward and backward traveling wave considering frequency dependent line parameters. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified with simulation test cases in PSCAD/EMTDC. Compared to the existing traveling wave direction criteria, the proposed method fully models the frequency dependent line parameters, and therefore presents higher sensitivity, reliability, and robustness independent of fault location, fault resistance, and measurement noise.

articleTitle: Real-time stability monitoring for power systems with renewable energy
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: There are various stability issues in power systems with high penetration of renewables and power-electronic equipment, such as wide-band oscillation, low inertia, and so on. This paper proposes a novel real-time stability monitoring method for power systems with renewable energy. The proposed method monitors synchronization, voltage, frequency, and oscillation stabilities with wide-band phasor measurement. Furthermore, a comprehensive real-time stability monitoring framework is established. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through simulation studies. The proposed stability monitoring framework is of great significance for ensuring the safe operation of power systems with renewable energy.

articleTitle: An improved short-circuit current control method for self-synchronization controlled wind turbine
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: The self-synchronization controlled wind turbine directly controls its output voltage amplitude and phase, which can actively support the grid frequency and voltage stability, provide inertia and damping support for the system, showing the characteristics of voltage a source. However, when the power grid fails, as this method has no current control loop, the short-circuit current of converter cannot be controlled, which may easily cause the damage of components due to the overcurrent. In view of the above problems, this paper conducts in-depth research on two short-circuit current control methods based on virtual impedance and voltage loop controller, analyzes their advantages and disadvantages, and proposes an integrated controller combine thesis two methods. The integrated current-limiting controller can realize the effective control of the steady-state and transient amplitude of the short-circuit current of the self-synchronization controlled wind turbine. The full electromagnetic transient simulation model of the permanent magnet direct-drive wind turbine is built, and the simulation verifies the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Research on new technology for on-line measurement of external insulation creepage distance
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: The creepage distance of the external insulation of high voltage equipment is an important parameter to ensure the safe operation of the power grid.At present,the measurement of creepage distance is carried out when the equipment is powered off.Manual measurement is required.The measurement data has large errors and the data verification cycle is long,which cannot meet the requirements of power grid equipment management.In this paper,three-dimensional laser scanning technology is used to detect the creepage distance of the external insulation.Accurate measurement data can be obtained,and the creepage distance live detection method is innovated.This new technology can be popularized and applied.

articleTitle: A non-unit adaptive traveling wave protection method for flexible DC transmission lines based on supplement of voltage data
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Traveling wave (TW) protection is crucial for ensuring the safety and stability of flexible DC transmission lines. Thereinto, shortening the sampling step is the key to improve the sensitivity of the derivative-based TW protection. However, higher sampling frequency is difficult to engineer and the protection performance will be constrained in case of the high resistance faults. To address this issue, a non-unit adaptive TW protection based on the supplement of voltage data has been proposed. Firstly, the voltage data is realized to complement utilizing the Lagrange's median theorem at the line boundary, which improves the sampling frequency. Then, it has been observed that the fault current variation is negatively correlated with transition resistance. Specially, the proposed protection takes this fully into account by incorporating the adaptive threshold that covers differences among various fault locations. Therefore, the proposed protection can effectively distinguish internal faults with high sensitivity. Finally, a two-terminal ±500kV MMC-HVDC (modular multilevel converter-high voltage direct current) system is built using PSCAD/EMTDC. The simulation results demonstrate that the line faults can be fast and correctly identified, even with 300 Ω fault impedance, in various fault scenarios.

articleTitle: Analysis of operating characteristics of power grid with offshore wind power integration under extreme weather conditions
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: With the steady growth in the proportion of newly installed offshore wind power, exploring the operating characteristics of power grids containing high proportion of offshore wind power under extreme weather conditions such as typhoon can help improve the structural design of wind turbines, the ability of power grids to withstand extreme weather events, and provide references for the selection of transmission equipment. In this paper, the operating characteristics of power grid with high penetration level of grid-connected offshore wind power under typhoon weather conditions are investigated in detail and comprehensively. Firstly, based on the actual historical meteorological data of typhoons, an uncertainty model of typhoon wind speed considering the spatial correlation is established by utilizing non-parametric Dirichlet process Gaussian mixture model (DPGMM). Then, based on the scenario analysis method, the probabilistic power flow (PPF) considering wind power and load uncertainties under different wind power penetration levels is conducted elaborately and systematically. In addition, the low-voltage ride-through and high-voltage ride-through under different fault disturbances are tested. Finally, the case studies are performed on the modified IEEE-39 bus system, and some useful conclusions can be obtained.

articleTitle: A protection strategy for DC microgrid based on the first derivative of line current spectrum energy using generalized S transform
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: DC microgrid technology has undergone significant growth due to advancements in renewable energy power generation and control technologies. Despite their flexibility and scalability, DC microgrids face vulnerability to fault currents due to the presence of numerous power electronic devices and complex operating conditions. Control systems further complicate fault current behavior, leading to potential malfunctions in protection devices. Thus, additional research is necessary to enhance the relay protection technology of DC microgrids. This paper presents a protection strategy utilizing the generalized S transform to analyze the first derivative of the current spectrum energy. By employing the generalized S transform, the line current spectrum energy before and after a fault can be obtained for different frequency bands. The obtained spectrum energy serves as the initiation criterion, while the first derivative of energy over time acts as the action criterion. Additionally, the voltage difference is employed as the pole selection criterion. To validate the proposed protection strategy, a DC microgrid system model is constructed on the MATLAB/SIMULINK simulation platform using a radial network configuration. A wind power system sending line is employed as a case study for simulation verification. The obtained simulation results demonstrate the selectivity and reliability of the proposed protection strategy.

articleTitle: Modelling and analysis of abnormal transient performance in bulk power system dominated by low-voltage-ride-through of distributed renewables
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Penetration of distributed renewable energy (DRE) is increasing in modern power systems. Integration of DREs have profound impact on transient voltage stability of bulk power systems, which has been observed in real-world power system event in USA and Australia. However, related studies are relatively rare in existing literatures. This paper utilizes a synthesis load model with renewables to study this issue. Two abnormal transient performances of DRE are revealed, which impact and interact with voltage of bulk power system. The performances are concluded as continuous low-voltage-ride-through (LVRT) of DRE and repeated LVRT of DRE, respectively. Sensitivities of the performances to DRE parameters are studied in weak power grid, with several novel and unexpected findings. Active power output of DRE significant influences the terminal voltage during LVRT, while impact of reactive output is not so prominent. Related results explain performance of several real power grids with high penetration of DREs.

articleTitle: Coordinated dispatch for seaport integrated energy-logistics systems with SOC-based clustering of electric trucks
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Seaport operating equipment is gradually developing towards electrification, and electric trucks are gradually applied to seaport logistics system. To achieve energy conservation, reduce emissions, and enhance the utilization of renewable energy, an optimization approach is proposed for seaport integrated energy-logistics systems. This approach aims to fully exploit the optimization potential of electric trucks and energy system integration. This paper investigates the energy consumption characteristics of transferring and charging electric trucks based on their operational characteristics. Furthermore, a coordinated dispatch model for SOC-based clustering of electric trucks and energy systems is established. This dispatch model can optimize seaport integrated energy-logistics systems by considering the task constraints of electric trucks and multiple forms of energy utilization, with the objective of minimizing operating costs. By optimizing the output of each unit and scheduling scheme of electric trucks, the energy system can achieve greater efficiency and cost savings. The proposed method effectively improves the economy of seaport integrated energy-logistics systems operation and utilization rate of renewable energy. It also reduces carbon emissions while ensuring the completion of the transfer task. This is demonstrated through optimization results using seaport operation data.

articleTitle: Categorized analysis of the response characteristics of EVs in Shanghai
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: With the increase in the scale of electric vehicles (EVs), the charging demands bring more challenges to the power grid. Ordered charging alleviates the impact of disordered charging and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology provides a measure to convert EVs from loads to dispatchable resources. In this paper, based on a statistic of newly licensed EVs in Shanghai, a categorized analysis of the response characteristics of EVs is conducted, and the dispatchable resource of the EVs is further modeled for the resource assessment in Shanghai.

articleTitle: The hybrid simulation step modelling approach for the CLCC based HVDC transmission system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: The commutation failure is one of the most significant and frequent problems affecting the operation stability and power quality of the line commutated converter (LCC) based HVDC system. In order to mitigate the commutation failure, a new type of controllable line commutated converter (CLCC) is proposed and implemented in the world's first CLCC project in China. However, the operation characteristics of the CLCC is causing the dynamic performance changes of the HVDC system due to the power electronic components contained, which brings a challenge to the simulation steps of the modelling of the whole CLCC based HVDC system. Therefore, this paper discusses a hybrid simulation modelling approach of the CLCC in order to accurately describe the steady and dynamic performance of the CLCC based HVDC system. The control scheme of the CLCC is also discussed to demonstrate the commutation failure mitigation method of the CLCC compared to the traditional LCC based transmission system.

articleTitle: Research on reactive power compensation and control strategy optimization of back to back DC project
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: The HVDC transmission system has played a very active role in promoting the intensive development of energy resources and large-scale optimal allocation in China, and realizing the interconnection and mutual benefit of power grids. As the back-toback DC project is located at the same converter station, the AC filter field covers a large area, and the AC filter area can also be appropriately optimized. This paper first analyzes the existing back-to-back DC control in detail, proposes the fixed reactive power control and instantaneous angle control strategy, and finally establishes the back-to-back simulation model in PSCAD, conduct the verification of transient voltage fluctuation and reactive power exchange and the simulation analysis of the whole process of power rise and fall, and verify the commutation failure that may be caused by the angle instantaneous control under multiple working conditions. The conclusion shows that the control strategy can suppress the transient voltage fluctuation of the filter switching after the capacity is increased within the required range, and can reduce the reactive power exchange during the process of power rise and fall, inhibit the oscillation phenomenon that may occur in the AC system connected to the weak receiver.

articleTitle: Research on collaborative optimization of wind farm power and yaw times based on yaw wake model
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Wake steering is one of the control strategies that can effectively reduce wake loss and improve wind farm generation. The upstream wind turbine sets a specific yaw angle so that its wake deviates from that of the downstream wind turbine, thus reducing the wake effect of the downstream wind turbine. Currently, an analytical wake model optimizes the yaw angle of a wind turbine, provided the wind direction is fixed. However, wind turbines operate in variable wind directions and the low yaw mechanism does not immediately track the optimized yaw angle. Therefore, this study proposes a dynamic yaw control method for wind farms with the goal of balancing the energy gain and the number of yaw actions.

articleTitle: Computational analysis of the fatigue of submarine cables affected by marine biological habitation
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: The fatigue life of submarine cables is key to the long-term safe transmission of energy at sea. In this paper, we investigate the effects of marine organisms when they host sea cables, computational analysis of biological growth on fatigue life of submarine cables. Includes marine life parasitic models, complex ocean conditions, biological habitation growth distribution, a computational model for the fatigue life of submarine cables under biological parasitic was developed by combining the rain flow counting method and the Miner damage criterion. Ability to evaluate the operational reliability of submarine cables, provides appropriate reference and supporting advice for the transmission of marine energy, maximize the safe operation of submarine cables.

articleTitle: Research on efficient consumption mode of distributed photovoltaic
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: The large-scale and rapid growth of distributed photovoltaic(PV) has an increasing impact on the safe and stable operation of distribution network as well as the safe power supply of users. In order to adapt to large-scale distributed PV access and improve the consumption level of PV, this paper studies the matching characteristics of distributed PV and power load and the proportion of energy storage configuration. The matching degree of load and PV output in different typical scenarios is compared, which provides a reference for the development of PV scenarios, and proposes energy storage configuration schemes in five typical scenarios.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of frequency regulation methods for a PV system without energy storage
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: With a higher penetration level of grid-connected PV systems, the frequency regulation ability of the power system has deteriorated due to the reduction of system inertia. There is an increasing need for PV systems to participate in system frequency regulation. This paper proposes a detailed comparative analysis of frequency regulation methods for a PV system without energy storage. Three categories of frequency support methods, including constant droop control methods, hybrid control methods combining droop control and virtual inertia control based on DC-link capacitor, and adaptive system frequency disturbance-based hybrid control methods, are described and analyzed in detail. To verify the performance of these methods, the PV system integrated into an IEEE 9-bus test system is simulated with EMTP-RV. These three methods are all separately implemented in the PV system. The performance of the analysis is demonstrated by comparing the results of these methods under various scenarios, considering the different PV penetration levels, irradiance levels, and load variations. The results show both advantages and limitations of these three methods, and the methods with dynamic control coefficients greatly perform on frequency regulation.

articleTitle: Diagnosis method of 500kV AC substation busbar break fault based on monitoring data
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Busbar is a crucial electrical equipment for collecting, distributing and transmitting electric energy. During the operation of substation, when the busbar has disconnection fault, it will change the distribution system, affect the accuracy of protection and voltage monitoring, and reduce the reliability of operation. In severe cases, it would lead to serious damage to equipment or large-scale power outage accident, which is harmful to the entire power system. The current busbar disconnection failure in 500kV AC substation is short of effective monitoring. This paper analyzes the characteristics of the power flow data when the busbar is disconnected, so that formulating the judgement methods and constraint conditions for busbar disconnection fault, which is based on the monitoring data of substation's equipment.

articleTitle: Transient stability analysis of grid forming-controlled converters considering three types of current limiting algorithms
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: By mimicking the primary frequency regulation or inertia response of synchronous generators, grid forming-controlled (GFMC) converters show similar external characteristics to synchronous generators. However, the inherent current limiting algorithms of GFMC converters lead to different transient stability characteristics compared with synchronous generators. In order to investigate the transient stability mechanism of GFMC converters with virtual synchronous generator control, power angle curve and phase portrait approach are used to give an intuitive analysis. The influence of voltage outer loop and three different types of current limiting algorithms----d-axis priority current limiting, q-axis priority current limiting and phase angle priority current limiting are given then. Base on PSCAD/EMTDC simulation test platform, the transient stability analysis proposed in this paper is verified by simulation results of GFMC converters under different operation conditions.

articleTitle: Hybrid energy storage adaptive compensation method for power fluctuations in the isolated microgrid
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: During the operation of isolated microgrids, high power periodic fluctuating loads can cause interharmonic power shocks and interharmonic current surges, which can lead to gas turbine bearing failures and endanger the operation of the isolated microgrid. Due to the variable power fluctuations, it is difficult to filter out interharmonic power with fixed filtering parameters. Therefore, the interharmonic power spectrum needs to be calculated as a basis for adjusting the filtering parameters and a hybrid energy storage system is added to match the filtering. As a result, a interharmonic power smoothing scheme based on power spectrum analysis is proposed. A bandpass filter is used in the frequency compensation section for accurate frequency selection, and the compensation frequency band is adaptively adjusted through power spectrum analysis. The scheme is able to reduce harmonic power shocks and enable the following of microgrid power change. Using the RT-LAB simulation platform to build the model, the results show that this method can achieve optimized coordination of hybrid energy storage, effectively suppress the interharmonic power fluctuations at the gas turbine, and enhance the stability of the isolated microgrid.

articleTitle: Low-carbon sizing for hydrogen storage system in an integrated electricity-heat-hydrogen microgrid considering waste heat of fuel cell
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: This paper proposes a low-carbon sizing method for a hydrogen storage system (HSS) in an integrated electricity-heat-hydrogen microgrid (IEHHM). To satisfy the diverse demands in the IEHHM, a low-carbon operating strategy is designed. Electric power, thermal power, and hydrogen are optimized coordinately to meet power demands and reduce carbon emission. A sizing optimization model for the HSS is presented based on the low-carbon operating strategy. The economy and carbon emission are balanced and minimized in the objective function. The waste heat and variant efficiencies of fuel cells are emphasized in the planning model. The waste heat can be recovered and utilized again to reduce energy consumption and carbon emission. The variant electric and thermal efficiencies of fuel cells help find the optimal operating point of fuel cells. A mixed integer linear programming is obtained. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated by case studies. Simulation results reveal that the total cost of IEHHM and the carbon emission reduces by over 12% when considering waste heat recovery of fuel cells.

articleTitle: Overview of research on compensation methods of temperature and humidity sensors in data room
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Data room temperature and humidity monitoring is crucial for server equipment and data security, but sensor errors often compromise the monitoring accuracy and stability. This paper reviews the compensation methods of data room temperature and humidity sensors based on multiple algorithms, such as artificial neural network (ANN) and time-frequency analysis, cubic spline difference and wavelet transform, adaptive fuzzy reasoning and Kalman filtering, and intelligent optimization algorithms. The paper compares the strengths and weaknesses of these algorithms in terms of efficiency, accuracy, adaptability, and scalability. The paper also discusses the future development trends and application scenarios of data room temperature and humidity sensor compensation, providing valuable insights and guidance for this field.

articleTitle: Influence of capacitive voltage transformer parameters on harmonic transmission characteristics
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Capacitive voltage transformer (CVT) has the advantages such as low insulation cost, small size and large electric field strength margin, so it is widely used in voltage measurement, relay protection and high frequency communication. However, CVT has the capacitors and inductors in its structure, these components are sensitive to frequency, so it can not accurately measure harmonics. Considering the stray capacitance and coupling capacitance of capacitive voltage transformer, the broadband response equivalent circuit model of CVT is established, and a cascade hierarchical analysis method is proposed to deduce the complete transfer function. On this basis, the influence of key parameters of CVT on harmonic transmission characteristics is simulated and analysed. The simulation results show that the increase of compensation reactor stray capacitance will make the resistance band move to the low frequency direction, the stray capacitance of the primary side of the intermediate transformer affects the attenuation degree of the high frequency band, and the effect of secondary side of transformer stray capacitance on the frequency response of CVT can be ignored. The results have reference significance for accurate harmonic measurement and manufacturing of CVT.

articleTitle: A study on the performance of a dual-raft wave energy convertor with mooring system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Wave energy is a vast and promising global resource with the potential to become the leading clean energy source worldwide, presenting a viable option for power generation. Among various wave energy converters (WECs), the raft-type device stands out for its high efficiency in capturing and utilizing wave energy. This research focuses on analyzing the dynamics of a two-valve body WEC based on a weakly nonlinear three-dimensional potential-flow theory. The device comprises two interconnected rectangular bodies with a power take-off system at the hinged point. The study investigates the impact of hinge position and spacing between floating bodies on the wave energy capture factor in the frequency domain, accomplished by employing equivalent power take-off (PTO) damping in lieu of linear damping. To validate the simulations, model experiments of WECs are conducted. Additionally, the study examines raft-type WEC mooring systems in the time domain and highlights the performance differences among various mooring systems through a comparative analysis.

articleTitle: Refined weather prediction model based on convolutional neural networks
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: The proportion of renewable energy in the energy structure is in a stage of rapid growth. With substantial increase in the installed capacity of wind power generation, fluctuation of wind power output will have a greater impact on an safe and stable operation of the power grid connected to the grid on a large scale. Accurate wind power forecasting is an important prerequisite to ensure an safe, stable and reliable operation of the power grid. Numerical weather prediction (NWP) is a key input of wind power forecasting. Improving the accuracy of numerical weather prediction has become one of the key factors to promote the development of wind power. Therefore, this paper comprehensively investigates the physical mechanism of atmospheric forcing and the seasonal difference of wind speed and analyzes the input parameters of the model and the division method of the sample set. Based on the analysis, a refined micro-scale artificial weather prediction model is constructed by convolutional neural networks. The model has demonstrated high accuracy in wind speed prediction at kilometer-level.

articleTitle: A novel method of steady-state modeling of self-excited induction generators based on state-space transient model and experimental validation
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: This paper presents a novel steady-state model based on transient equivalent circuits and state-space mathematic model in two-phase stationary reference frame of the loaded self-excited induction generator (SEIG) employed in distributed generation system driven by multiple renewable energy sources. The proposed method is able to significantly improve performance of efficiency and quality of computation for comprehensive parameters of SEIG systems. Unlike the existing techniques, the novel method takes into account both of the transient and steady-state parameters as well as the stator voltage dynamics from both of the mathematic and motion views that there exist solutions corresponding to and represented by a certain characteristic value for the dynamic equation. Theoretical analysis and good agreement between computed results and experimental results confirm the feasibility of the proposed method and demonstrate the novel steady-state model superior performance.

articleTitle: Stability oriented chance constrained optimal power flow in isolated microgrids
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: The uncertain nature of renewable energy sources (RESs) always brings negative impacts on the system stability especially in microgrids. In this paper, we propose a stability-oriented chance constrained optimization model for incorporating the uncertainties of RESs outputs. In this model, the upper level aims to minimize the expected generation cost without violating the stability chance constraint, the lower level concerns about the stability index. Then, we assume that the RES output uncertainties follow Gaussian distribution and hence reformulate chance constraints into linear deterministic versions. With linearized constraints in hand, the bi-level model can be solved by Benders decomposition-based approach. Simulation results on the 33-bus microgrid reveal that compared to other benchmarking approaches, the proposed model has the capability of converging in much shorter CPU time with adopting the sensitivity cuts. The proposed model converges 10 times faster with more accurate solutions. Moreover, the stability index is dramatically enhanced as well as the benefit for bus voltage security.

articleTitle: Influence of resonance mechanism on the performance of Solar Thermoacoustic Generator
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: In this paper, the resonance mechanism and its effect on the performance of Solar Thermoacoustic Generator (STAG) are studied by theoretical analysis and simulation. The coupling among acoustic, mechanical and electrical resonances in STAG system is investigated in detail, and its consequent influence on the optimisation of STAG design is presented. To achieve this, an improved mathematical model of STAG is built, in order to overcome the drawbacks of previously published models which were built only from acoustic aspect, and which do not explain adequately the coupling between thermoacoustic engine and linear alternator and the influence of vibration control technique on the STAG performance.

articleTitle: Voltage disturbance compensation control of DFIG-based wind turbins during asymmetric faults in weak AC grid
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Weak grid asymmetric faults can result in complex interactions between the doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG)-based wind turbines and the grid through positive and negative sequence coupling paths, leading to system instability. In order to improve the stability of the DFIG system under such adverse condition, a harmonic linearization method is firstly used to model the sequence impedance of DFIG system. Accordingly, the impact of positive-sequence active current on system stability is studied. Then, a voltage disturbance compensation control strategy is proposed. According to the generalized Nyquist stability criterion, the proposed voltage perturbation compensation control can significantly improve the stability of the DFIG system. Finally, the accuracy of the theoretical analysis is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Analysis of the impact of MMC-HVDC DC side fault on AC side
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: MMC-HVDC is one of the most critical ways to transmit renewable energy over medium and long distances. When a fault occurs on the DC side, it affects the voltage and current on the AC side, and there is a lack of research on the DC fault propagation mechanism. Therefore, in this paper, the AC-DC coupling characteristics of MMC converters are analyzed in depth and the underlying causes of the mutual influence are revealed. Further, based on existing MMC projects, the AC-side voltage and current trends under different fault conditions and DC-side fault clearance methods are analyzed. The adaptability of traditional distance protection is also analyzed. The influence boundary of DC faults is clarified to provide a theoretical basis for subsequent AC/DC protection.

articleTitle: Research on carbon flow distribution considering power data synchronization error
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Power data synchronization error is unavoidable, and the influence of synchronization error on carbon flow distribution has not been taken into account in the existing studies. A mathematical model for calculating carbon flow distribution is established based on the theory of power flow analysis. On this basis, the relationship between synchronization error and carbon flow distribution is explored. An example is designed to verify the influence of synchronization error on carbon flow distribution. The simulation results show that the synchronization error affects the carbon flow distribution of the system by changing the power demand of nodes. Finally, the thesis is summarized.

articleTitle: Optimization strategies for virtual power plants' participation in high penetration renewable energy systems' day-ahead scheduling
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: With the gradual reduction of conventional fossil fuels, the development of renewable energy has experienced rapid growth. The increasing penetration of renewable energy in the distribution grid presents new challenges and issues for its safe and stable operation. This paper proposes a day-ahead optimization scheduling strategy for the participation of virtual power plants (VPP) in high-penetration renewable energy systems. Firstly, the integration of renewable energy generation systems, energy storage systems, electric vehicles, and flexible loads is consolidated into a unified virtual power plant. Subsequently, a day-ahead optimization scheduling model is formulated, considering the involvement of the virtual power plant in the distribution grid. Finally, simulation calculations are performed on a modified IEEE33 node system. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the high-penetration renewable energy system facilitated by VPP participation. This system not only enables electricity trading but also optimizes the utilization of internal resources, thereby enhancing the reliability of power supply and effectively promoting the integration of new energy sources.

articleTitle: Hardware-in-loop simulation and operation control characteristics of offshore wind power integrated via VSC-HVDC system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: The dynamic and transient characteristics of power electronic converters are greatly affected by the time-varying nonlinearities of control systems. Considering the complicated multi-layer control units and untransparent strategies, the control systems of wind generators and VSC-HVDC can hardly be accurately simulated through digital modelling. In this paper, a hardware-in-loop (HIL) simulation platform of offshore wind power integrated via VSC-HVDC system is constructed. The control systems of wind generators, offshore converter station, and onshore converter station are simulated by real control devices, while the rest electrical equipment is modelled in the real-time digital simulator (RTDS). The control devices are connected to the RTDS by analog and digital IO interfaces or optical fiber communication through the AURORA protocol. Based on the proposed HIL simulation platform and industrial parameters, the dynamic characteristics of wind power integrated via VSC-HVDC system can be analysed and evaluated.

articleTitle: Analysis of the sudden increase in dissolved acetylene content in oil of ultra high voltage converter transformer
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Analyze the cause of the sudden increase in dissolved acetylene content in oil of UHV converter transformer. Through various methods such as on-site partial discharge testing, the application of high-frequency, ultrasound, sound-vibration joint detection technology to locate abnormal signals, combined with internal inspection of the transformer, the main reason for this abnormality is that the metal bolts connected to the shielding ring on the grid side of the grid side outlet device (lower part of the grid side riser) are not reliably connected, resulting in suspended discharge.

articleTitle: DBN-GRU-based short-term load forecasting for integrated energy campus considering dynamic coupling characteristics
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Multivariate load forecasting technology is the key cornerstone to ensure the supply and demand balance and stable operation of integrated energy systems (IES). However, the IES load with strong randomness and volatility aggravates the difficulty of accurate prediction of ultra-short-term multivariate load. Therefore, an optimal bagging ensemble ultra short-term multivariate load forecasting method a multi-level deep learning algorithm by combining the Deep Belief Network (DBN) and Gate Recurrent Unit (GRU), which was verified on the actual campus dataset. Firstly, the Nadam optimizer is used to improve the DBN network and directly mine the depth features from the original data. Secondly, starting from the campus energy management system, collect historical samples of different supplies supply and demand. Then, the typical characteristics of multi-energy demand are analyzed, including peak-to-peak ratio, a strong correlation between calendar, weather, eigenmode component set, calendar rules, meteorological environment, and load data; Then, based on DBN-RELM, a combined forecasting model is established.

articleTitle: Inertia configuration method to enhance frequency stability of power grids considering the spatial distribution characteristics
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: When a disturbance occurs in the power grid, the frequency of the grid changes. It is essential to make sure that the grid frequency following specific disturbances stays within safety limits. In the early stages of the frequency response following a disturbance, the rate of change of frequency (ROCOF) is the most critical parameter for indicating frequency stability and the inertia is the dominating impact factor. A well-designed configuration of system inertia can help enhance frequency stability to make meet requirements. This paper first examines the spatial distribution of system frequency after a disturbance, and based on this analysis, proposes an optimal inertia allocation method. Specifically, this model increases node inertia by incorporating energy storage at strategic nodes. By ensuring a certain total amount of added inertia, the proposed model aims to minimize the maximum ROCOF possible. Finally, simulation tests conducted on IEEE 68 BUS show that the proposed method can effectively reduce the maximum ROCOF following a disturbance, which ensures the power grid's safe operation.

articleTitle: Research on DC feeder protection of novel metro traction power supply system based on model parameter identification
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: The novel traction power supply system is an important component of new power system, with new characteristics of high proportion of distributed power sources, high proportion of impulsive loads, and high proportion of power electronic device access. Therefore, the protection of DC feeder is crucial for its stable operation. However, due to the complex fault characteristics in the new system and the impact of locomotive start-up current, traditional DDL protection is no longer applicable. Therefore, researching new protection methods suitable for this system is urgent and challenging. This paper proposes a new DC feeder protection principle based on model parameter identification. This scheme utilizes the charging and discharging characteristics of inductance, ignoring the line inductance at the peak current of the feeder and calculating the equivalent impedance of the line at that moment. A new protection principle is constructed by comparing the difference in equivalent impedance between faults and locomotive start-up current. Extensive simulation results show that the proposed protection method can not only identify faults in different sections but also effectively distinguish locomotive start-up current, achieving fast and reliable protection operation.

articleTitle: Passive based control for PV-battery DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: For the characters of photovoltaic (PV) of strong randomness and uncertainty, the status of energy storage equipment is becoming more and more important in the DC microgrid. Therefore, this article adopts passive based control (PBC) method to control the energy storage converter, and then PI controller to perform voltage and current double closed-loop control. Analyze the performance of PBC controller through simulation and verify the effectiveness of PBC control. Under the conditions of sudden light changes and sudden load changes, simulations verify that the independent PV-energy storage system has excellent steady-state performance and dynamic performance under the PBC-SMC compound control method.

articleTitle: Optimal scheduling strategy for photovoltaic-storage system considering photovoltaic forecast error and short-term fluctuation limitations scenario analysis
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Energy Storage Systems (ESS) play an important role in smoothing out photovoltaic (PV) forecast errors and power fluctuations. Based on the optimization of energy storage (ES) to smooth out the PV forecast error and power fluctuation, the optimal scheduling strategy of the PV-ESS with the analysis of PV output forecast error and power fluctuation scenarios is proposed. First, the PV power is sampled at different moments during the override control cycle, and the typical sampling scenarios are classified by K-means and GAN optimization. Then, based on the classification results, we calculate the upper and lower limits of ES margin at the current control moment and solve the whole PV-storage scheduling model by MPLI optimization method with the minimum value of PV power crossing penalty as the objective function on this basis. Finally, a refined segmented linearized battery storage life loss model is developed to consider the economics of ES technology in improving the smoothing of PV power uncertainty.

articleTitle: Online monitoring and analysis system for steel structure safety of offshore wind farm booster station based on multi-source data
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Aiming at the current industry pain points of the independence of dynamic monitoring and static monitoring systems in the safety monitoring of steel structures in booster stations of offshore wind power plants on the market, as well as the low degree of intelligence and accuracy, this paper studies the establishment and modification methods of real-time calculation models for steel structures in booster stations, and simulates and analyzes the stress, mode, deformation relationships, and mathematical models among structural safety accidents of booster stations under multiple operating conditions, A structural safety analysis method for booster stations integrating multiple online monitoring data is proposed, which can effectively and intuitively analyze the internal parameters and safety status of the steel structures of the booster stations. A Windows application software, "Online Monitoring and Analysis System for Structural Safety of Booster Stations in Offshore Wind Power Plants," has been developed and applied to a 300MW offshore wind power plant booster station renovation project in Rudong County, China, to monitor the safety status of its steel structures.

articleTitle: Real-time control strategy research for electric vehicle clusters participating in frequency regulation ancillary services
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: With the development of demand response technologies, electric vehicles (EVs) can be centrally dispatched through the concept of virtual power plant(VPP) to participate in frequency regulation and ancillary services. To address the challenges posed by multiple uncertainties and user demands, this paper presents a research on real-time control strategy for intelligent building-type VPP participating in frequency regulation ancillary services. Firstly, EVs are aggregated into intelligent building-type VPP, and a virtual battery model is utilized to establish a power margin model for assessing their frequency regulation potential. Subsequently, based on power margin consistency, a decentralized exact first-order algorithm using a projection-based approach is employed to achieve power allocation for frequency regulation among different buildings. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is validated through case studies, demonstrating that EV clusters can effectively participate in frequency regulation ancillary services while ensuring user demands and improving resource utilization.

articleTitle: An identification method of new energy output and typical outgoing curve characteristics
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: It is necessary to identify the characteristics of different curves in the process of power system dispatching and formulating mode strategy, so as to screen out typical curves for calculation. The identification of curves is generally based on the concept of graphical similarity, while for power system power curves, the overall similarity cannot be considered alone, as its temporal characteristics are equally important. Aiming at the particularity of power curves in power systems, this paper proposes a classification method for new energy curves, outgoing power curves, and load curves, and proposes a definition method for such distances, as well as a calculation method for the matching degree between curves.

articleTitle: Parametric study of a self-reacting point absorber intergrated with a magnetic bistable mechanism and a mechanical motion rectifier
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: This paper investigates the parameters of the magnetic bistable device (MBD) and the mechanical motion rectifier (MMR) of a scaled power take-off (PTO) assembled in a self-reacting point absorber (SRPA). The MBD generates a bistable restoring torque by combining gyration magnets and fixed magnets, and the MMR converts the relative reciprocating linear motion of floats into a unidirectional rotation, thereby mitigating the fluctuations of the output power. Both the snap-through characteristic of MBD and the disengagement characteristic of MMR have an overall improvement effect on the first and second grade conversion efficiency of the wave energy device. This research lays the foundation for the subsequent bistable mechanism research, and engineering application of wave energy devices.

articleTitle: Research on the topology of multiphase interleaved bidirectional DC-DC converter for energy storage system
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Based on the traditional bidirectional Buck/Boost DC converter, the multiphase interleaved parallel bidirectional converter can be obtained by using the multiplex technology, which can reduce the input current ripple of the low voltage side and prolong the battery life. However, if the device parameters or control parameters between the modules are inconsistent, the current circulation will appear in the converter. In order to reduce the circulation between modules, the main circuit with the coupling inductance is analysed in the paper. First, in Buck mode and Boost mode, the circuit diagram of each working mode is established respectively, then the inductance and capacitance parameters in the main circuit are designed, and last, the simulation model of the main circuit is established to verify the correctness of the theoretical analysis and the selection of main circuit parameters. The simulation results indicate that the bidirectional converter of the energy storage system can obtain a large power increase at a small cost by using the multiplex technology, and if the inductance of bidirectional converter adopts the form of coupling inductance, the current circulation between modules can be reduced effectively.

articleTitle: Analysis of the near-fundamental-frequency oscillation in an actual renewable energy system transmitted through MTDC grid
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: Near-fundamental-frequency oscillation (NFFO) events were observed in a renewable energy system (RES) connected to a four-terminal direct current (MTDC) grid in China, which has the world's largest DC transmission network. The sending terminal of the MTDC grid includes various converter-interfaced generators, such as permanent magnetic synchronous generator (PMSG), doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG), and photovoltaic (PV). The oscillation phenomenon is unique since the NFFO frequencies of 44 Hz and 56 Hz are relatively close to the fundamental frequency. For the first time, field-measured data are employed to investigate the oscillation characteristics. The analysis indicates that a resonance circuit (RLC) exists between the wind farm and the MTDC, and the wind farms display negative resistance at the oscillation frequencies. Further investigations identify the oscillation source based on the distribution of power flow at the oscillation frequencies. The paper also explores potential causes and countermeasures for the observed phenomena.

articleTitle: An operational strategy of variable speed pumped storage units considering system flexibility
publicationTitle: 12th International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2023)
abstract: With the continuous increase in the installed capacity proportion of new energy units, the volatility and uncertainty of their output pose a great challenge to the flexibility of the power system. Compared with conventional pumped storage units (CPSU), variable-speed pumped storage units (VSPSU) have a wider operating range and higher efficiency. In order to clarify the advantages of VSPSU in typical application scenarios, this paper conducts research on how to use VSPSU to improve power system flexibility. Power system flexibility refers to the ability of a power system to quickly respond to significant fluctuations in supply or load. Thus, this paper firstly introduces a power system flexibility calculation method considering uncertainty and converts it into corresponding economic benefit indicators.
